newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot product diffs end steady, NYMEX firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot product diffs end steady, NYMEX firms.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product differentials ended near steady Friday in very subdued trade, with many market players absent after the Chistmas holiday earlier this week.

Outright prices gained on the back of the NYMEX strength, with heating oil up 0.49 cent by the settlement and gasoline up 0.23 cent. Market watchers attributed that strength to the weekly American Petroleum Institute report, which showed draws in both distillates and crude oil.
New York Harbor (NYH) heating oil diffs were talked lower initially, though few buyers emerged to pick up barrels.
NYH prompt No. 2 heating oil for was offered at 0.20 cents under the screen initially, but illiquidity in the market prevented barrels from changing hands.

U.S. Gulf (USG) No. 2 heating oil for the back 36th cycle on the Colonial pipeline was talked between 6.26 and 5.75 cents under the screen as sellers pulled back, and early January material was talked between 4.25 and 4.50 cents under the print.
Activity should increase next week, traders said, when many players return to work.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
